title: Alice node children are subprotocols
statement: Let $X,Y,	ext{ and }[0m\alpha$ be types, let $f:X\to\{0,1\}$, and let $P$ assign a protocol over these types to each bit. For every bit $b$, the child protocol $P(b)$ is a subprotocol of the Alice node determined by $f$ and $P$.
hypotheses_covered: A function from Alice's input type $X$ to a bit
A protocol-valued function on the two bits
replaced:
Let $f : X \to \{0,1\}$ be an Alice decision function and let $P$ assign a protocol
$P(b)$ to each bit $b$. Then for every bit $b$, the child $P(b)$ is a subprotocol of the
Alice node $\texttt{alice}\; f\; P$.
